title: Finding
description: A single security finding as it moves through DETECTED -> CANDIDATE -> TRIAGED -> VERIFIED -> CONFIRMED (or REJECTED / NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE). See CLAUDE.md 'Finding Lifecycle' and agents/security-verifier.md.

id.description: Stable identifier. Temporary during review (e.g. a UUID or scanner-provided id); assigned final SEC-NNN form at 15_final_report.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Only CONFIRMED findings appear as confirmed vulnerabilities in the final report.

title.description: Short, specific description of the vulnerability (not a CWE name alone).

category.description: Vulnerability category, e.g. 'SQL Injection', 'Broken Object Level Authorization', 'Hardcoded Secret'.

owasp_category.description: OWASP Top 10 / API Top 10 category, when applicable. See knowledge/owasp/.

severity.description: Technical and business impact. Distinct from priority -- see config/severity.config.yaml.

priority.description: Remediation urgency, assigned in 11_security_prioritization. See config/priority.config.yaml.

priority_factors.description: Auditable breakdown of what drove the priority assignment.

confidence.description: How much of the source-to-sink path and security controls were actually confirmed.

location.description: Primary affected location. Use 'locations' instead when deduplication merges multiple call sites of the same root cause.

locations.description: Used when deduplicate_findings.py merges multiple occurrences of the same root cause.

source.description: Where attacker-influenced data originates (e.g. 'HTTP query parameter `id`').

sink.description: The dangerous operation the data reaches (e.g. 'raw SQL query execution').

data_flow.description: Traced path per the SOURCE -> ... -> SINK model in CLAUDE.md.

confirmed.description: Whether this step was actually verified in code vs. assumed.

evidence.description: Actual code excerpts and/or scanner output supporting the finding -- not paraphrases.

attack_vector.description: How an attacker delivers the exploit (e.g. 'crafted HTTP POST to /api/orders/{id}').

exploitation_scenario.description: Concrete, narrative walkthrough of an actual exploitation, not a generic description of the vulnerability class.

business_impact.description: Consequences in business terms: data exposure, compliance, financial, reputational.

kev.description: CISA KEV correlation for dependency findings. See scripts/scanners/check_kev.py.

verification.description: The 'Independent Verification' evidence layer, populated by security-verifier during 09_independent_verification. Kept separate from 'dynamic_validation' below -- static/independent-verification confidence and dynamic-validation confidence are never merged into one number.

dynamic_validation.description: The optional 'Dynamic Validation' evidence layer, populated by pentest-validator during 10_dynamic_pentest_validation -- only present when that stage ran (requires config/pentest.config.yaml to be enabled with an authorized target; see agents/pentest-validator.md). Absence of this field means dynamic validation was not attempted, not that it failed.

target.description: The authorized target tested against, per config/pentest.config.yaml.

authorization_reference.description: Which allowlist entry authorized this test.

confidence_impact.description: How this result changed the finding's confidence, and why.

related_architecture_recommendations.description: ARCH-NNN recommendation IDs whose implementation would address this finding's structural root cause. Informational cross-reference only -- does not replace this finding's own remediation.

false_positive_analysis.description: Required whenever status is REJECTED, and useful documentation even when CONFIRMED (why the obvious FP explanations don't apply here).
